events.title: House of Representatives Elects John Quincy Adams
events.description: No candidate won a majority of electoral votes in the 1824 election, so the US House of Representatives decided the presidency. It chose John Quincy Adams over Andrew Jackson, who had won more popular and electoral votes.
events.significance: The result fueled Jackson's claim of a 'corrupt bargain' and reshaped American party politics. It helped Jackson's supporters build the Democratic Party.

events.title: Death of Fyodor Dostoyevsky
events.description: The Russian novelist died in St. Petersburg at age 59. He wrote Crime and Punishment, The Idiot and The Brothers Karamazov. Russia's Julian calendar then dated his death January 28.
events.significance: Dostoyevsky's psychological and philosophical novels shaped modern literature, existentialist thought and the way writers portray the inner life.

events.title: Volleyball Is Invented
events.description: William G. Morgan, a YMCA physical education director in Holyoke, Massachusetts, created a new game he called 'Mintonette'. He designed it as a gentler indoor alternative to basketball for older businessmen.
events.significance: The game was later renamed volleyball. It grew into an Olympic sport played recreationally and competitively around the world.

events.title: The Beatles Appear on The Ed Sullivan Show
events.description: The Beatles made their first live US television appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show, just days after arriving in America. An enormous TV audience tuned in.
events.significance: The broadcast launched the 'British Invasion' of American pop music. It marked a turning point in popular culture.

events.title: The Boeing 747 Takes Its First Flight
events.description: The first Boeing 747 'Jumbo Jet' took off from Everett, Washington. It was the largest passenger airliner in the world at the time.
events.significance: The 747 made long-distance air travel affordable for millions of people. It transformed global tourism and commerce.
